title: Tattoo Knowledge Base - Styles, Techniques, Application, Placement
description: Consolidated and de-duplicated from style.txt, klasyfikacja.txt, and technics.txt. This is the craft reference the agent draws on for style alignment (flow phase 3), technique selection, and image-prompt vocabulary. Each style/technique carries render_tags: short keywords to drop into an image prompt.

american_traditional.description: Bold black outlines, a limited but vibrant palette, iconic imagery: eagles, hearts, anchors, roses, pin-ups, nautical themes.
american_traditional.history: Emerged in 1930s USA from sailor and military culture.

neo_traditional.description: Evolution of American Traditional: richer detail, broader palette, decorative motifs, more dimensional shading.
neo_traditional.history: Late 20th century, blending traditional roots with modern illustration.

old_school.description: Simple, iconic designs, thick lines, minimal shading, restricted color.
old_school.history: Early-20th-century Western tattooing; predecessor to American Traditional.

new_school.description: Cartoonish, exaggerated forms, bright saturated color, graffiti and hip-hop influence.

black_and_grey_realism.description: Lifelike rendering in grayscale, emphasis on shadow, contrast, and fine detail.

color_realism.description: Full-color lifelike depiction; demands advanced blending and technique.

portrait.description: Realistic faces of people or animals; captures expression and nuance.

micro_realism.description: Miniature yet highly detailed realism; needs fine needles and a steady hand.

blackwork.description: Solid black ink used for bold, graphic, often abstract or ornamental designs.

dotwork.description: Image built from thousands of dots; density controls shade and depth. Meditative, rhythmic.

geometric.description: Lines, circles, triangles, and symmetrical patterns; sacred-geometry influence.

solid_black_blackout.description: Large areas fully saturated in black, often for dramatic coverage or cover-ups.

linework.description: Design carried entirely by line; can be intricate or minimal.

japanese_irezumi.description: Large, flowing, colorful compositions with mythological creatures, koi, dragons, waves, and florals; strict traditional rules and deep symbolism.
japanese_irezumi.history: Developed in the Edo period; deeply tied to Japanese culture.
japanese_irezumi.cultural_note: Style is widely practiced, but certain motifs carry specific meaning - respect symbolism.

tribal.description: Bold black symmetrical patterns from various Indigenous traditions.
tribal.cultural_note: Generic 'tribal' borrows from living cultures - check origin before copying.

maori.description: Ta moko: spirals and koru patterns encoding heritage, genealogy, and status.
maori.cultural_note: RESTRICTED / sacred. Ta moko is a closed cultural practice - do not copy. Offer respectful, inspired abstraction only.

polynesian_samoan.description: Intricate motifs (waves, turtles, tiki, spearheads) telling stories of status and lineage.
polynesian_samoan.cultural_note: Culturally significant. Approach with respect; inspired abstraction preferred over literal traditional marks.

haida.description: Pacific Northwest formline: black geometric forms and animal motifs.
haida.cultural_note: Indigenous closed practice - inspired abstraction only.

chicano.description: Mexican-American culture: fine black-and-grey line, lettering, religious and portrait motifs.

aztec_mayan_egyptian.description: Ancient-civilization iconography, glyphs, and deities rendered graphically.

watercolor.description: Soft, fluid washes and splashes mimicking watercolor painting; often paired with a line or ink 'anchor'.

sketch_style.description: Raw, hand-drawn look with visible construction lines and loose shading.

trash_polka.description: Chaotic collage of realism and abstraction, typically black and red.

biomechanical.description: Fusion of organic anatomy and machinery; sci-fi, cybernetic, Giger-influenced.

surrealist.description: Dream-logic imagery, imperfect symmetry, imaginative juxtaposition.

graffiti.description: Street-art influence: bold color, stylized lettering, spray-paint texture.

horror.description: Dark, macabre imagery from horror and gothic aesthetics.

three_d.description: Illusion of depth via shading and perspective; the piece appears to lift off or sink into the skin.

minimalist.description: Clean, understated designs; few lines, restrained detail.

fine_line.description: Delicate, precise thin linework; subtle shading; ideal for small, personal, elegant pieces.

illustrative.description: Storybook / editorial illustration crossed with tattoo craft.

lettering_script.description: Typographic art from elegant script to bold graffiti fonts.

ornamental_mandala.description: Symmetrical decorative patterning, lace, mandalas, filigree.

abstract_brazilian_fusion.description: Non-linear shapes, flamboyant color, high contrast - Alexei's Rio-influenced signature.

white_ink.description: Subtle, light designs in white ink; scar-like, understated.

glitch.description: Digital-distortion aesthetic, RGB shift, datamosh feel.

marble_smoke_fire.description: Effect-driven renders: marble veining, wispy smoke, dynamic flame.

negative_space.description: Untouched skin becomes part of the image; the design is defined by what is NOT inked.

shading.soft_shading: Gradual, blurred shadow transitions for smooth gradients.
shading.hard_shading: Bold, defined shadow with strong contrast edges.
shading.whip_shading: Fast, tapering flicks of the machine for dynamic, grainy texture.

linework.fine_line: Thin, delicate lines for subtle, detailed designs.
linework.bold_line: Thick, strong outlines for high-impact, long-lasting designs.
linework.broken_line: Interrupted lines for an artistic, sketch-like or unstable effect.
linework.continuous_line: A single flowing, uninterrupted line - minimal and elegant.

color.black_and_grey: Monochrome shading using diluted black ('grey wash') and pure black.

texture_and_effect.dotwork_pointillism: Image built from dots; density = shade.
texture_and_effect.brush_stroke: Painterly strokes emulating a loaded brush.
texture_and_effect.etching_engraving: Cross-hatched, carved look reminiscent of engraving.
texture_and_effect.silhouette: Solid filled shapes defining a subject by outline.

application_methods.machine: Standard coil or rotary machine tattooing.
application_methods.hand_poked_stick_and_poke: Manual needle-and-ink, no machine; slow, textured, intimate.
application_methods.tebori: Traditional Japanese hand-poking with a rod of needles; associated with Irezumi.

classification_axes.note: Tattoos have no single universal taxonomy. Useful axes for reasoning about a request:
classification_axes.by_style: Traditional, Realism, Abstract, Biomechanical, Cultural, etc.
classification_axes.by_technique: Linework, Shading, Color Packing, Dotwork, Freehand.
classification_axes.by_culture_region: Maori, Samoan, Aztec, Japanese, etc. (mind closed/sacred practices).

forearm.notes: Great flow along the arm; sun exposure fades color over time.

upper_arm_shoulder.notes: Large muscle canvas; ages well; good for bold work.

ribcage.notes: Emotional placement; breathing movement; needs steady sessions.

back.notes: Largest canvas; epic multi-session storytelling; healing logistics.

sternum_chest.notes: Symmetrical designs read well; intimate/self-directed meaning.

hand_fingers.notes: Fades and blurs fastest; fine detail is risky long-term; career-visibility conversation.

calf_thigh.notes: Good for large or fine work; thigh ages well.

neck_throat.notes: Strong social/career implications - discuss honestly before committing.
